Link two or more records in your {{< var vm.product >}} inventory together. Dependencies are useful to understand how a record is
affected by or affects other records in your inventory.

::: {.attn}

## Prerequisites

- [x] {{< var link.login >}}
- [x] There are two or more records registered in the inventory.[^1]
- [x] You are the record owner[^2] for the record you want to set interdependencies for, a [{{< fa code >}} Developer]{.bubble}, or assigned another role with sufficient permissions to perform the tasks in this guide.[^3]

:::

## View interdependencies

1. In the left sidebar, click **{{< fa cubes >}} Inventory**.

2. Select the type of `{Record}` you want to view interdependencies for by clicking on **{Record} Inventory**.[^4]

3. Select a record or find your record by applying a filter or searching for it.[^5]

4. On the record details page, click the **Interdependencies** tab to view an interactive flowchart:

    - The currently viewed record is highlighted with a blinking animation.
    - Click and drag to change what area is displayed on the flowchart.
    - To zoom in and out, use your mouse scroll button or zoom trackpad gesture.
    - Turn on **Display Artifacts** for an artifact type to add that type's artifacts to the flowchart.
    - When a record-to-record link has a dependency type,[^dep-types] the connecting line is labeled with it, for example `Data Source (Upstream)`.

5. Below the flowchart, the **Interdependencies** table lists the same linked records and artifacts as the flowchart, with a **Type** column showing the record type or artifact type of each row:

    - Click **Manage Columns** to add any core, custom, or stakeholder field of the linked records or artifacts. Columns are labeled `Record:` or `Artifact:` so the same field on each side stays distinct, and a column that does not apply to a row shows a gray dash.
    - Add the **Dependency Type** column to show the type assigned to each record-to-record link.
    - Save a combination of columns and displayed artifact types as a view, for yourself or shared with your organization, the same way you save inventory views.[^views]

### View dependencies across the inventory

To see dependencies without opening each record, add the **Upstream Record IDs** and **Downstream Record IDs** columns to the inventory listing with **{{< fa table-columns >}} Manage Columns**.[^inventory-columns] Each shows the comma-delimited IDs of the record's direct dependencies, kept in sync automatically when a dependency is added or removed. Records you do not have access to are left out of the list.

- Filter the listing by these columns with the **in** or **not in** operators to find every record that has a specific record upstream or downstream, for example `Upstream Record IDs in M_5475`. Matching is on the exact ID.
- Both columns are included in the inventory CSV export[^export] and in scheduled data exports[^data-exports] when selected.
- In Analytics, the **Inventory Record - Dependencies** dataset has one row per dependency, so you can chart which records are most depended on. Group or filter by **Dependency Direction** so each relationship is counted once.[^analytics]

## Edit interdependencies

1. In the left sidebar, click **{{< fa cubes >}} Inventory**.

2. Select the type of `{Record}` you want to edit interdependencies for by clicking on **{Record} Inventory**.[^6]

3. Select a record or find your record by applying a filter or searching for it.[^7]

4. On the record details page, click the **Interdependencies** tab.

5. Click **{{< fa square-plus >}} Manage Dependencies** to open up the interdependencies detail menu.

6. Select either the **{{< fa arrow-up >}} Upstream** or **{{< fa arrow-down >}} Downstream** tab:

    - **Upstream** — Provides input or intermediate results to another record.
    - **Downstream** — Receives input and typically performs further processing, predictions, or actions based on that input.

    You can swap between the **{{< fa arrow-up >}} Upstream** or **{{< fa arrow-down >}} Downstream** tabs to set both interdependency types at once.

7. On your list of related records from the inventory, add or remove interdependencies as desired:

    - **Add** — Select the checkbox for any records that are either upstream or downstream dependent on the current record.
    - **Remove** — Unselect the checkbox for any records previously linked as upstream or downstream dependent on the current record.

    Use the search box or **{{< fa filter >}} Filter** to narrow the list with the same rule builder as the inventory listing. The list loads one page at a time; selections you make on one page are kept as you move to another.

8. (Optional) For each selected record, choose a **Dependency Type** from the list your organization has defined.[^dep-types] If your organization requires a dependency type on every link, **Save** stays unavailable until every newly selected record has one.

9. Click **Save** to apply your changes.

Once applied, interdependencies will populate on all linked records.

## Define dependency types

Dependency types describe what kind of relationship a record-to-record link is, such as a data source or a challenger model. They appear on the flowchart, in the **Interdependencies** table, and as a choice in **Manage Dependencies**.

::: {.callout}
To define dependency types, you must be a [{{< fa hand >}} Customer Admin]{.bubble} or assigned another role with sufficient permissions.[^3]
:::

1. In the left sidebar, click **{{< fa gear >}} Settings**.

2. Under {{< fa cubes >}} Inventory, select **Interdependencies**.

3. Add, rename, or delete dependency types as needed. Deleting a type keeps the links that used it and removes the label from them.

4. (Optional) Select **Require a dependency type on every link** so that new links cannot be saved without one. Links saved before the requirement stay valid.
